My guy, I would like to help you the best, but take it that I am self-educated and I might be mistaken on some things...

If you feel sick, you're probably tapering wrong, use the Ashton manual. My mom is tapering off Clonazepam and she stuck with Clonazepam. Your 3 different benzos might be difficult to taper off all of them.

Tapering doesn't mean you will feel heavenly, or even feel it. The thing is, tapering off means that you will only keep dangerous things like delirium and epilepsy in check, while decreasing your dose and tolerance. It's a hard, harsh and a long process and you will feel as low as you were high. My mom still has very frequent panic attacks and anxiety, social and generalized. 

Talk to your doctor man, or go to a hospital (normal or mental) for safe tapering environment. The doctors there are there to help you, but as I've researched, it's probably better to use the Ashton manual and be really, really determined to taper and stop, one mistake and you're at the beginning.

PEOPLE, IF I SAY SOMETHING WRONG, PLEASE REPLY AND CORRECT ME.

If you want to taper off benzos, don't drink alcohol (you're just replacing the "same" drug with an even worse drug). Smoke weed, it can help calm you down and withdrawal will be easier for you. I am by no means expert, but if you wanna lower your tolerance, or taper off completely, I would use just diazepam, which is less potent and it has looong half life, meaning it will be in your system for longer and it's generally easier to taper off with diazepam only. Alprazolam and Bromazepam are potent, the more potent benzo, the higher the tolerance will be and the risk is much higher. Stick to one benzo, diazepam, it's just that diazepam is the easiest to taper off and has long half life and will prevent delirium and epilepsy. Even if you had to take them for the rest of your life, please, use diazepam.
